answer.rationale: Memory_73 explicitly warns that promotional pricing materially reduced 30-day retention and should not be generalized—this disqualifies it despite leadership pressure. Memory_57 shows referral incentives performed well in established customers with qualified revenue lift and no measurable retention harm, making it the most aligned with sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Memory_31 and memory_86 confirm SMB segment responsiveness to friction reduction, supporting a combined approach. Referral incentives leverage existing customer base to acquire qualified accounts during competitive pressure, avoiding the retention cliff that promotional pricing created. A standard_experiment scale allows rapid deployment to at-risk SMB cohorts while limiting downside risk. This preserves uncertainty by testing before broad rollout and avoids the documented pitfall of aggressive pricing mechanics.
